what_it_does: AI accelerators that work on sparse data (matrices or tensors where most values are zero) store only the nonzero numbers, which come in rows of varying length. Standard on-chip fast memory (a scratchpad inside the chip) is organized in fixed-size slots, so a short row wastes most of a slot while a long row spills across many — both situations waste capacity. SeaCache solves this by packing short rows together and splitting long rows across slots to fill them efficiently. It also needs a smart policy for deciding which rows to keep in the scratchpad when it runs out of space; the optimal theoretical rule requires expensive bookkeeping, so SeaCache approximates it cheaply by exploiting the regular patterns in how sparse AI computations access data. Finally, it dynamically adjusts how much of the scratchpad is devoted to data versus to the bookkeeping records themselves, measuring the best balance at runtime.
